newsitem.title: USA: Transatlantic crudes still scant on US Gulf Coast.
newsitem.headline: Transatlantic crudes still scant on US Gulf Coast.

text.p: Transatlantic barrels remained scant on the U.S. Gulf Coast on Tuesday as a result of the closed arbitrage, traders said.
The spread between benchmarks West Texas Intermediate/Cushing and North Sea Brent was around $1.20-25 a barrel Tuesday afternoon, wiping out the economic incentive for most transatlantic trade.

One U.S. refiner, however, is offering West African Qua Iboe, Brass River and Cabinda/Nemba cargoes loading at the end of February. The refiner is asking around dated Brent plus $2.10-20 a barrel for the Qua Iboe and Brass River, while the Cabinda/Nemba is being offered on an fob basis plus freight, traders said.
Meanwhile, Latin American activity was quiet amid pre-Lenten festivities.
A European company sold two Vasconia cargoes loading in mid-March at an unconfirmed discount to WTI/Cushing of around $3.15 a barrel, traders said.
One market watcher, contesting the market talk, suggested the actual price was between $3.35 and $3.50 a barrel.
Separately, a U.S. Gulf Coast refiner is reselling a prompt Vasconia cargo, raising speculation among traders of possible refinery problems.
Colombian crude trade so far seemed unaffected by an ongoing general strike in the country, although traders were monitoring the situation closely for any sign of impact on the ports.
